newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian Radenska says 1996 net down 7.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian Radenska says 1996 net down 7.4 pct.

text.p: Slovenian mineral water producer and health resort operator Radenska said on Tuesday its 1996 preliminary net profit eased to 547 million tolars ($3.5 million) from 591 million in 1995.
"Profit was down due to higher taxes and a colder summer when sales of non-alcohol drinks were down," chief executive Alojz Behek told Reuters.
Sales of mineral water and other non-alcohol drinks represent about 60 percent of the company's total sales.
Behek said the company's preliminary group sales rose to 12.5 billion tolars from 10.8 billion a year ago.
The number of guests in the two health resorts operated by Radenska rose three percent to 230,000, with foreign visitors representing 44 percent of all guests.

Behek said the 1996 dividend would be determined at a shareholders' meeting scheduled for late August or early September, but added it would be at least 46 tolars per share, compared to 46.73 tolars a year earlier.
Radenska's total investment rose to $8.7 million in 1996 from $5.8 million a year before.
"Investments were up mainly due to an the extension of the Radenci health resort swimming facilities," Behek said.

He said current year investment was expected to reach about $5.8 million, while sales and net profit should rise about 10 percent respectively. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439 ($ = 157.3 Slovenian Tolars)
